body: Vali is one of the best Turkish movies. It is not the best, but it deserves a very important place... We are living in a world where crime, money and lies are in every corner of our lives and Vali shows us an important part of these lies. The acting was fine, the music was fine and the camera was also fine. Nothing did disturb me, unless the ugly truth... The movie could be a bit more longer, because at the end you have the feeling that not everything was shown enough. The movie has a good story that could be turned into a longer movie. This is my only complain... I recommend it to everyone and especially for Turks.....

From a cinematic perspective, the film relies heavily on dialogue and character-driven storytelling. The focus is less on dramatic spectacle and more on illustrating the governor's philosophy and administrative approach. While this strengthens the film's political and social message, it sometimes slows the pacing and reduces the level of dramatic tension.

One of the strongest aspects of the film is its portrayal of leadership as a moral responsibility rather than merely a bureaucratic position. The character of Yazicioglu embodies the idea that effective governance requires courage, empathy, and a willingness to challenge established systems. However, critics have noted that the film occasionally idealizes its central figure, presenting him almost as a heroic symbol rather than exploring more complex or critical dimensions of his career.

Overall, Vali: The Governor is an important film in Turkish political cinema. By portraying the life of Recep Yazicioglu, it raises broader questions about public administration, leadership, and the relationship between the state and society. Although the film sometimes leans toward admiration rather than critical analysis, it remains a meaningful tribute to a public servant who left a significant mark on Turkey's administrative history.
